newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen give up Nikkei - driven gains,end flat.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen give up Nikkei - driven gains,end flat.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures ended a subdued session little changed on Wednesday after giving up most of their afternoon gains.
Euroyen futures were briefly pulled up following a short-squeeze in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures when Tokyo stocks failed to extend their gains from Tuesday's rally.

The Bank of Japan's tight money market operation for the second day and an overnight decline in U.S. bonds kept Japanese interest rate futures languishing on the lower end of their range for much of the morning.
"The Euroyen futures eventually picked up on the back of the JGBs. But they look mixed. There was not much aggressive follow-through buying," said a trader at a European institution.
The benchmark March Euroyen contract finished unchanged from its CME close at 99.07, after reaching a high of 99.11. December JGBs settled at 121.40 against their previous 121.30.
Eurodollar futures had an even less inspired session, with the March contract ending at 93.76 against its IMM close at 93.77 on measly volume of 7,690 lots.

Dealers said the market would scrutinise August wholesale and consumer inflation releases, due on Thursday and Friday respectively, for clearer indications of the Federal Reserve's expected stance at its September 24 meeting.

"From now until the 24th, any figure that comes out good will raise the possibility of a rate hike," said the dealer, adding however, that the Fed was unlikely to put rates up by more than 25 basis points.
U.S. treasuries were sold off overnight on renewed fears of a rate hike after Federal Reserve governor Janet Yellen said the U.S. economy had entered an "inflationary danger zone."
